implementation intention

description.value: Participants used a pre-trained implementation intention to regulate their emotional response to disgust- or sadness-eliciting images. When the cue word REAPPRAISE appeared, they told themselves that the images were just pixels on a screen and could not affect them; when SUPPRESS appeared, they used the if-then response to block out bad feelings and stay cool. The if-then cue-response plan was intended to promote automatic response initiation and reduce deliberation.

spans.text: goal intention

description.value: Participants used a general goal-intention emotion-regulation strategy while viewing disgust- or sadness-eliciting images. For REAPPRAISE trials they adopted a detached and unemotional attitude; for SUPPRESS trials they tried to stop themselves from becoming emotional and suppress their feelings. The strategy required deliberate, effortful regulation without a pre-specified cue-response link.

spans.text: attend

description.value: Participants viewed disgust-, sadness-, or neutral-eliciting images naturally, allowing any feelings elicited by the image to occur, without applying an emotion-regulation strategy.

instructions.value: Participants viewed disgust-, sadness-, or neutral-eliciting images preceded by instructions to attend, reappraise, or suppress. Attend trials required viewing naturally and allowing feelings to occur. Regulation trials required using either a goal-intention strategy or an implementation-intention strategy. Goal-intention participants were instructed to adopt a detached and unemotional attitude for reappraise trials or try to stop themselves becoming emotional for suppress trials. Implementation-intention participants were instructed to use if-then plans linking the cue word to a specified response, such as treating the images as pixels or blocking out bad feelings and staying cool, and then rated how sad or disgusted they felt.
